cases.label: FlashAttention-2 arithmetic complexity
cases.question: A colleague claims that FlashAttention-2 reduces exact attention's arithmetic complexity from quadratic to linear and therefore guarantees a tenfold speedup on every GPU. Does the paper support either claim? Explain what actually produces its speedups and identify the hardware and workloads supporting the reported results. Does the paper report measurements on an NVIDIA H100? If not, explicitly state that the requested measurement is unavailable rather than estimating it.

cases.label: Longformer local and global attention
cases.question: How does Longformer combine local and global attention? Explain which tokens receive global attention, how that choice depends on the task, and how information can propagate between distant tokens. Under what assumptions does its attention complexity scale linearly with sequence length? Cite the relevant original passages.

cases.label: Performer approximation versus exact attention
cases.question: Does Performer compute exactly the same attention outputs as standard softmax attention on every forward pass? Explain what FAVOR+ approximates, the role of random features, and the theoretical guarantees stated in the paper, including their assumptions. Separate approximation guarantees from empirical results and cite the supporting evidence.

cases.label: Transformer architecture and experimental evidence
cases.question: Summarize this paper's research problem, proposed architecture, main contributions, experimental setup, key results, and limitations. Explain the roles of self-attention, multi-head attention, and positional encoding. Support the summary with citations to the original paper, and distinguish demonstrated results from broader claims.

cases.label: Transformer translation results and limitations
cases.question: Summarize the research problem, method, translation results, and conditions under which the results apply in this paper. Explicitly identify what the paper leaves unaddressed. Cite the paper for each factual claim.

cases.label: FlashAttention method and evidence
cases.question: Summarize the motivation, algorithm, experimental evidence, and limitations of FlashAttention. Explain how its IO-aware design reduces GPU memory traffic and memory usage. Distinguish arithmetic complexity, memory consumption, and measured runtime. Include the experimental conditions for any speedup figures you report, and support key claims with original-paper citations.

cases.label: Three linear-attention approaches
cases.question: Review how Linformer, Linear Transformer, and Performer reduce the cost of attention. Compare low-rank projection, kernel feature maps, and random-feature approximation. Discuss their assumptions, theoretical guarantees, autoregressive inference mechanisms, and empirical limitations. Include a cited comparison table and explain why sharing linear complexity does not make these methods mathematically equivalent.

cases.label: Five efficient-attention papers
cases.question: Write a literature review of these five papers on efficient attention. Organize the discussion by technical approach rather than presenting five disconnected summaries. Compare sparse attention, low-rank approximation, random-feature approximation, and IO-aware exact attention. Cover mechanisms, assumptions, arithmetic complexity, memory costs, experimental evidence, and limitations. Include a comparison table with citations covering every paper. Distinguish theoretical efficiency from measured speed and explicitly disclose any gaps in paper coverage.

cases.label: Detailed FlashAttention GPU mechanisms
cases.question: Analyze how FlashAttention-2 improves upon FlashAttention. Compare their approaches to GPU memory access, tiling, parallelism, and work partitioning. Explain whether either method changes the mathematical attention operation or its asymptotic arithmetic complexity. For each reported speedup you discuss, identify the hardware, sequence length, workload, and baseline. Include a cited comparison table, and do not combine speedup figures from incompatible experimental settings.

cases.label: Two-paper FlashAttention overview
cases.question: Review these two papers together. Explain the main idea of FlashAttention and how FlashAttention-2 improves upon it. Summarize their shared goal and the most important differences, using evidence from both papers.

cases.label: LoRA and QLoRA memory reduction
cases.question: Find the original LoRA and QLoRA papers. Compare their core methods and explain how each reduces GPU memory use. Present the comparison in a table and cite the relevant paper for each entry. Avoid direct numerical comparisons across different experimental settings.

cases.label: Self-evolving Agent skills
cases.question: Find representative papers on how agents evolve their own skills. List the papers and, for each one, briefly explain how the agent uses experience to update existing skills. Base each explanation on evidence from the paper.

cases.label: Sparse attention for long documents
cases.question: Find and review three to five research papers on sparse attention for long-document language processing. Identify distinct attention patterns and explain how they balance local connectivity, long-range information exchange, and computational cost. Use original full-text evidence, not search snippets alone. Provide a source list, a cited comparison table, and a synthesis of recurring limitations and open questions. If fewer than three papers can be accessed, report the coverage gap explicitly.

cases.label: Hallucination detection and reduction
cases.question: Explore how researchers detect and reduce hallucinations in large language models. Review relevant papers and summarize the main approaches, findings, and remaining challenges.

cases.label: Retrieval-augmented knowledge-intensive QA
cases.question: Investigate how retrieval-augmented generation helps language models answer knowledge-intensive questions. Summarize the main ideas, recent developments, and common limitations based on relevant papers.
